newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks ignore Dow, slip on rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks ignore Dow, slip on rate fears.

text.p: Mexican stocks opened slightly higher on Tuesday bolstered by the Dow Jones, but quickly entered negative turf on jitters over high money market rates, traders said.
"Yesterday's strong close was a little artificial and dealers are nervous over the way money market rates soared yesterday," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index .MXX was off 8.18 points in early trade, or 0.22 percent, at 3,790.27.
Trading volume was cautious at 8.5 million shares, but still heavier than for many recent sessions.
Another trader put the early slide in blue chips down to profit-taking.

"There was much speculative buying at the close yesterday so some prices are sliding on profit-taking. Mild U.S. inflation data helped. Even though blue chips are down, I see buyers and the broad market is mixed rather than down," he said.
Telecom Telmex weighed most on the downside, with its L shares off two centavos to 16.04 pesos after reaching an early high of 16.10 pesos. Telmex ADRs were nonetheless up 5/8 to 40-5/8.
Financial group GFB was the most heavily traded stock .AV.MX and was up three centavos on what traders said was a technical rebound after a sharp fall on Monday.
On the broad market, of 55 stocks traded, decliners marginally outnumbered gainers by 20 to 18.
